requirements.title: Constants are literal or named and may be referenced but not redefined
requirements.definition: A constant, as cross-referenced to 6.2.3, is a literal constant or a named constant. A literal constant is a scalar syntactic form indicating type, type parameters and value. A named constant is a constant with a name that has the PARAMETER attribute under 8.5.13 or 8.6.11. A reference to a constant is always permitted, and redefinition of a constant is never permitted.

pending.literal-constant-reference: PENDING complete program using integer, real, logical and character literal constants in value contexts with independent PRINT/IF literals. The oracle is the exact expected literals and reached execution; no mutable storage or compiler-folding claim is the evidence.
pending.named-constant-reference: PENDING complete program declaring INTEGER,PARAMETER :: k=81 and CHARACTER(*),PARAMETER :: c='ok', then referencing both in value contexts. The oracle is literals 81 and 'ok' after reached execution; the declarations must precede the references per 8.5.13.
pending.parameter-attribute-source: PENDING paired positive plans for type-declaration PARAMETER and PARAMETER statement forms, each with a constant expression and a later reference. The oracle is the independently computed literal value, and the plan records whether 8.5.13 or 8.6.11 supplied the PARAMETER attribute.
pending.constant-subobject-reference: PENDING complete program with a named constant array or character constant and references to an element or substring in expression context only. The oracle is the selected literal element/substring after reached execution; no defining context is used.
pending.constant-redefinition-prohibited: PENDING source-only diagnostic/control plan attempting to define a named constant or its subobject in an assignment context, repaired to use an ordinary variable initialized to the same value. The repaired program observes the new assigned literal; the invalid program is not executed, and any numbered diagnostic ownership by 9.2 C901 or assignment rules must be recorded separately.

requirements.oracle: Source-qualified paired plans and positive-control admissions, with any future executable observation delegated to the owning semantic requirement. A literal expected value or fixed inquiry result is stated only where the future program first establishes definedness and execution of the relevant path.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The permission to reference a constant is not a claim that every occurrence is valid in every syntactic context, and the redefinition prohibition is not treated as an automatic numbered-constraint-style diagnostic duty here. All entries are PENDING plans only; no case, execution, oracle, source-use link, fixture approval or coverage claim is created.

review_rationale: Independent source review in doc/source_audits/batch_087.json reads the original 9.3 paragraph and its six fine units and confirms its four distinct assertions: a constant is a literal or named constant, a literal constant is a scalar whose syntactic form indicates type, type parameters and value, a named constant has a name with the PARAMETER attribute under 8.5.13 and 8.6.11, and a reference to a constant is always permitted while redefinition never is. The redefinition prohibition is recorded here as the owning prose, with actual diagnostic ownership left to C901 and the assignment and definition-context rules elsewhere. All five facets remain pending source plans; no case, execution, oracle or fixture approval is created.
